name: NY-26
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Tim Kennedy running with $1.2M cash on hand
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~96%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Kennedy: a D+11 district, incumbency, and a large fundraising edge over a challenger with no reported money. Markets price this as a near-certain Democratic hold, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Hannon or an unexpectedly favorable national environment could narrow the margin, though an upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Tim Kennedy, the Democratic incumbent in this Buffalo-area district, seeks another term after winning the seat in a special election. The district leans Democratic by about eleven points, and Kennedy enters the general election with a substantial financial advantage, having raised over $2.3 million and holding $1.2 million on hand. Republican challenger Dennis Hannon has no reported fundraising or outside support.

With no public polling of the race and no expert ratings, the outlook rests on fundamentals, which favor Kennedy decisively. Prediction markets also price a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
